Purpose: Tall infographic or diagram, explains a process, system, or concept visually. Default style is clean editorial infographic — see scene-variants/editorial.json.

Style.Genre: Clean editorial infographic — like a magazine or technical blog diagram
Style.Rendering: Flat vector-style illustration with subtle paper-grain texture, clean lines, soft drop-shadows. NOT cyberpunk, NOT photorealistic, NOT painterly.

Lighting.Type: Flat ambient, no dramatic light sources, no glow
Lighting.Shadows: Very subtle soft drop-shadows under panels for gentle depth — no high contrast

Primary: Soft slate blue (#007acc) for outlines and the title
Accents: Warm amber/orange (#f59e0b) reserved for focal badges and key callouts
Light cool grey (#9ca3af) for secondary/harness labels
ColorPalette.Treatment: Mostly white with thin coloured outlines. Amber appears only on focal-point badges so it reads as the editorial focal accent. Everything else is restrained black-text-on-white.

Effects: No glow, no neon, no scanlines, no holographic effects
Flat clean shapes with thin 1–2px outlines
Atmosphere.Mood: Calm, clean, editorial — fits a serious technical blog post, not a sci-fi poster

PromptKeywords: minimal colour palette — black text on white with soft blue outlines and amber accent badges
CRITICAL: every text label must be spelled exactly, no letter substitutions, no missing or doubled letters

CompositionNotes.Background: Pure white #ffffff across the full canvas — no gradient, no texture, no border
CompositionNotes.Framing: Pure flat-illustration infographic, no human figure, generous white margins around the content so it breathes
CompositionNotes.SubjectPlacement: Content flows top-to-bottom (or whichever direction fits the diagram type), with comfortable spacing between elements
CompositionNotes.DepthOfField: Flat, all elements crisp and readable
CompositionNotes.Layout: Clear visual flow with numbered or connected elements; title at top, optional slim legend at bottom
CompositionNotes.TypographyTreatment: Clean sans-serif (something like Inter, Helvetica, or system-ui). Section headings in medium-weight all-caps or semibold. Body labels in regular weight. Titles in semibold.

DiagramTypes.Name: Process Flow
DiagramTypes.Description: Vertical flowchart of rounded-rectangle nodes connected by thin grey chevron arrows. Focal nodes use blue outline + amber badge; de-emphasized nodes use grey outline + grey label.
Elements: Optional loop-back as thin dashed grey curve

DiagramTypes.Name: Comparison
DiagramTypes.Description: Two columns or panels side-by-side, each with the same node structure so differences read at a glance.

DiagramTypes.Name: Hierarchy
DiagramTypes.Description: Stacked layered panels showing nested or containment relationships.

DiagramTypes.Name: System Map
DiagramTypes.Description: Nodes and connections showing relationships between components — feedback loops drawn as thin dashed grey curves.
Elements: Clusters grouped by light grey containers

UseCases.Name: Concept Explanation
UseCases.Description: Breaking down a complex idea into visual steps with named panels

UseCases.Name: Before/After
UseCases.Description: Showing transformation or improvement via matched-structure comparison panels

UseCases.Name: Mental Model
UseCases.Description: Illustrating how to think about something via hierarchy or system map

optimistic.AccentAdjustment: Use the warm amber sparingly on outcome/result panels; consider one small soft-green check icon as a positive marker

analytical.AccentAdjustment: Lean on the blue/charcoal palette; reserve amber only for the single focal point you want the eye to land on first

frustrated.AccentAdjustment: Use a muted warning amber on the blocked/broken node, with all other panels in plain grey outline — let the colour do the work

contemplative.AccentAdjustment: Drop amber accents almost entirely; let the diagram be quiet, mostly outlined panels on white
